intro: I turn complex business problems into products, intelligent systems and scalable operations.

Previously at Amazon, I led initiatives to improve customer engagement, product adoption and operational efficiency. Today, through ARCHMATION, I help companies solve business problems using AI and automation.

projects.title: Turning declining engagement into sustained product usage.
projects.problem: Daily engagement was declining: active users had fallen from approximately 50,000 to 35,000. The original Question of the Day offered a reason to open the app, but did not consistently connect that visit with meaningful progress.
projects.discovery: Behavioural and product data pointed to friction in getting started, difficulty choosing relevant activities and weak reasons to return. The opportunity was to reduce decision effort and connect short sessions with the next useful action.
projects.decision: I proposed Daily Digest: short personalised sessions combining behavioural nudges, habit formation, relevant practice and clear next actions, rather than another feed of content.
projects.approach: I defined the core journey and personalisation logic using activity, progress, weak areas and goals. I worked with product, UX, research, ML, engineering and content teams on the experience, notification strategy and iterative improvements.
projects.outcome: Previously reported DAU recovered from approximately 35,000 to 80,000+. Reported retention increased by 32% and session duration by 64%. These are observational product metrics, not controlled causal estimates.
projects.assurance: I monitored engagement and retention after launch and used the results to prioritise improvements. Leadership made final feature decisions.
projects.summary: I transformed a declining daily engagement feature into a personalised experience, increasing return visits, retention and adoption of other product features.

chapters.label: Executive summary
chapters.title: Executive summary
paragraphs: Amazon had built an extensive learning ecosystem, but getting students to return regularly and discover relevant product features remained a challenge.

I identified the underlying barriers and proposed Daily Digest, a personalised daily experience combining behavioural science, relevant recommendations and short, actionable activities. I led the definition of the product logic and user journeys, collaborating with cross-functional teams on execution and continuous improvement.

chapters.label: Product context
chapters.title: Product context
paragraphs: Daily active users had declined from approximately 50,000 to 35,000. The existing Question of the Day served as an entry point to the product but lacked personalisation and meaningful connections to other features. I saw an opportunity to transform it into a driver of customer engagement, retention and broader product adoption.

chapters.label: Customer research
chapters.title: Customer research
paragraphs: I analysed customer behaviour and research findings to understand why students were not engaging consistently despite having access to an extensive learning library.
Three primary barriers emerged:
• Time constraints: Students were balancing school, coaching and examination preparation.
• Decision friction: Students struggled to identify what to study or practise next.
• Perceived value: Students wanted immediate, relevant assistance with their individual weaknesses and examination preparation.
These insights informed the core product requirements for Daily Digest.

projects.title: Scaling personalised counselling through AI.
projects.problem: Scaling individual university admissions counselling requires reducing repetitive documentation and planning effort without compromising personalisation or counsellor judgement.
projects.discovery: I examined student profiling, consultations, documentation, planning and follow-ups to identify opportunities for context-aware decision support.
projects.decision: I defined three connected capabilities: Transcript Intelligence, Intelligent Counselor Workbook and Personalized Student Planning Engine.
projects.approach: I developed product strategy, workflow requirements, decision logic, evaluation requirements and implementation planning. The planning engine proposes feasible next steps based on goals, eligibility, prerequisites and time constraints.
projects.assurance: Source traceability, privacy, incomplete or contradictory information, feasible recommendations and counsellor approval were explicit product requirements.
projects.outcome: The advisory deliverables define an interconnected product architecture and implementation direction for Athena’s teams. Deployment and commercial impact are not claimed.
projects.summary: I developed an AI product strategy to increase counselling capacity without compromising personalisation. The strategy focused on reducing repetitive work, leveraging institutional knowledge and enabling better student-specific decisions.

chapters.label: The business challenge
chapters.title: The business challenge
paragraphs: Athena’s college admissions counselling model relies on understanding each student individually and guiding their academic and extracurricular development over several years. Increasing counselling capacity without compromising this personalisation was the central business challenge.

chapters.label: Understanding the problem
chapters.title: Understanding the problem
paragraphs: I examined the activities surrounding each counselling session. Counsellors spent time reviewing previous discussions, documenting conversations, updating Airtable records, tracking student commitments and researching suitable academic and extracurricular opportunities.
Another opportunity was Athena’s accumulated knowledge: approximately ten years of counselling recordings, documents and student records that could inform future counselling decisions.

chapters.label: Defining the solutions
chapters.title: Defining the solutions
paragraphs: I identified three specific areas where AI could support counsellors.

Transcript Intelligence — Convert counselling recordings into structured session summaries, extracting student interests, decisions, commitments and deadlines. Counsellors review the extracted information before updating student records.

Intelligent Counsellor Workbook — Maintain an evolving student profile covering academic progress, interests, achievements and pending activities. Before each session, counsellors receive a summary of previous discussions, outstanding commitments and changes in student circumstances.

Personalised Student Planning Engine — Recommend courses, competitions, internships and research opportunities based on student interests, academic goals, existing skills and availability. Check eligibility, prerequisites and deadlines before generating individual activity plans.

chapters.label: Architecture and product decisions
chapters.title: Architecture and product decisions
paragraphs: I proposed structured databases for student records, RAG for retrieving historical counselling knowledge and explicit business rules for eligibility and activity scheduling.

The reliability requirements addressed specific failures: invented student information, contradictory records, unsuitable opportunities and unrealistic time commitments. Consequential recommendations and record changes required counsellor approval.

chapters.label: From strategy to implementation
chapters.title: From strategy to implementation
paragraphs: I developed the product requirements, solution architecture and implementation roadmap, recommending that Athena begin with session documentation before introducing automated student profile updates and personalised planning.

projects.title: Building the intelligent backbone of a startup.
projects.problem: A recruitment technology startup needed to make institutional knowledge easier to access, reduce repetitive coordination and establish a more systematic approach to early customer adoption.
projects.discovery: The opportunity was to create reusable AI capabilities across teams rather than disconnected prompts, with explicit ownership, approval and evidence requirements.
projects.decision: I structured the work around an intelligent knowledge base and employee assistant, an Agent Backbone for operations, an Agent Backbone for software development, and GrowthOS for acquisition.
projects.approach: I defined use cases, requirements, workflow logic, qualification rules and acceptance criteria. AI-assisted prototypes covered knowledge retrieval, requirements drafting, engineering planning and evidence-led prospect research.
projects.assurance: The common reliability approach included source grounding, deterministic validation, human approval and representative tests. Commercial acquisition and deployment outcomes are not established.
projects.outcome: Functional prototypes and product specifications demonstrated selected workflows, including planning, validation and approval. Broader production integration remained a separate engineering responsibility.
projects.summary: I developed a unified AI framework connecting organisational knowledge, business workflows, software development and customer acquisition within an integrated operating model.

chapters.label: The business challenge
chapters.title: The business challenge
paragraphs: WhiteTable was developing its product while establishing its internal operating processes. I examined how teams documented decisions, communicated requirements, planned work, collected customer feedback and approached customer acquisition.
I identified opportunities to improve these processes through shared organisational knowledge and reusable AI workflows.

chapters.label: Understanding the problem
chapters.title: Understanding the problem
paragraphs: Documentation was fragmented, meetings and decisions were not consistently recorded, and customer feedback lacked a structured collection process. Internal communication, work planning, task ownership and follow-ups required better coordination.

Software development lacked standardised PRDs, requirement specifications and consistent development workflows. Customer acquisition involved repetitive prospect discovery, research and outreach preparation.

chapters.label: Defining the solutions
chapters.title: Defining the solutions
paragraphs: Organisational Intelligence — I developed a knowledge framework and prototyped an employee assistant to retrieve information about the company, product, technical architecture and internal processes. The proposed knowledge workflows would capture meeting notes, decisions and customer feedback, keeping information accessible across teams.

Agent Backbone — Business Operations — I defined reusable agent workflows for meeting summaries, action-item tracking, customer feedback classification, work planning and internal reporting. Outputs from one activity could inform subsequent work.

Agent Backbone — Software Development — I designed workflows to translate product requirements into structured PRDs, technical specifications, implementation tasks and acceptance criteria. The PRD Creator and Work Planner workflows connected Google Drive documentation with Jira work items. Agents would work within defined responsibilities, with validation and approval before consequential changes.

GrowthOS — Customer Acquisition — I prototyped workflows for prospect discovery, company research, prospect qualification and personalised outreach preparation, with structured records to track prospects and previous interactions.

chapters.label: Architecture and reliability
chapters.title: Architecture and reliability
paragraphs: I defined shared components for knowledge retrieval, task orchestration, structured outputs and validation.
The prototypes explored how agents could exchange information, prevent duplicate records, validate outputs against requirements and flag failures for human review.

chapters.label: My contribution
chapters.title: My contribution
paragraphs: My work covered business problem identification, AI strategy, solution architecture, workflow definition, functional prototyping and testing. These capabilities were intended for progressive integration into WhiteTable’s operations.

projects.title: Building innovative learning products at scale.
projects.problem: During BYJU’S rapid expansion from its flagship app launch, the product needed consistent learning experiences across subjects, grades and formats while coordinating multidisciplinary teams.
projects.discovery: Scaling required a shared structure for learning objectives, content specifications, interactive experiences and review—not simply increasing production volume.
projects.decision: I focused on knowledge architecture, guided learning journeys, interactive STEM and repeatable production processes.
projects.approach: I led and collaborated across subject experts, product, design, art, engineering and production teams. The work connected concept-level specifications to videos, assessments, games, simulations and guided experiences.
projects.outcome: The work supported the expansion of digital learning products and repeatable multidisciplinary delivery. The programme-scale outputs describe team contributions rather than individual production.
projects.assurance: Subject-matter validation, common specifications and coordinated quality reviews were foundational.
projects.summary: I played a key role in building and scaling BYJU’S learning products during its rapid growth, leading multidisciplinary teams across product development, knowledge architecture, interactive learning and large-scale operations.

chapters.label: Building during rapid business growth
chapters.title: Building during rapid business growth
paragraphs: I joined BYJU’S before the launch of its flagship learning app and contributed to its product expansion over the following five years. As the business expanded across grades, subjects and product formats, my responsibilities grew from specialised team leadership to multidisciplinary product development and operations.
The expanding product portfolio required new capabilities, shared product frameworks and development processes that could support multiple initiatives simultaneously.

chapters.label: Establishing a common product foundation
chapters.title: Establishing a common product foundation
paragraphs: As the product ecosystem grew, connecting learning resources, assessments and individual user journeys became increasingly complex.

I led the development of a knowledge architecture across Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics and Biology, defining concept relationships, prerequisites and resource mapping. This provided a common foundation for product personalisation, recommendations, assessments and guided learning journeys.
The framework allowed different teams to develop products using a shared underlying structure.

chapters.label: Developing new product capabilities
chapters.title: Developing new product capabilities
paragraphs: I led and contributed to initiatives that expanded the capabilities of the learning platform:
Guided journeys: Structured pathways connecting instruction, practice, assessment and remediation.
Assessment intelligence: Performance analysis, identification of knowledge gaps and targeted recommendations.
Interactive products: Educational games, simulations, applets and virtual laboratories.
Experiential learning: Physical learning kits and flipped-classroom pilots connecting digital products with classroom instruction.
My responsibilities covered defining product requirements, developing experience frameworks and coordinating execution across specialised teams.

chapters.label: Building organisational capabilities
chapters.title: Building organisational capabilities
paragraphs: Rapid product expansion required teams with expertise in subject knowledge, product development, design, media and technology.

I established multidisciplinary development workflows, product specifications, resource allocation processes and quality standards. These enabled teams to execute multiple product initiatives in parallel while maintaining consistency across the expanding product portfolio.

chapters.label: Contribution to business expansion
chapters.title: Contribution to business expansion
paragraphs: Over five years, I played a key role in establishing product capabilities, knowledge systems, teams and development processes that supported BYJU’S rapid growth.
My contribution extended across product innovation, capability building and operational execution at scale.

projects.title: Simplifying business operations through AI and automation.
projects.problem: Routine internal questions, scattered procedures and outstanding task follow-ups consume employee and manager attention.
projects.discovery: The opportunity is to improve access to approved information and task visibility without introducing another complex operating system.
projects.decision: I formulated three lightweight workflows: employee onboarding and training, searchable internal SOPs, and task visibility with reminders.
projects.approach: The design uses a shared training and SOP repository, a central task tracker for owners and due dates, and n8n to route reminders through WhatsApp and Gmail. WhatsApp is for notifications, not training or the authoritative record.
projects.assurance: Approved sources, escalation for unanswered questions, a single authoritative task record and human responsibility for completion and exceptions.
projects.outcome: The workflow design establishes a practical implementation direction using existing tools. Deployment, adoption and quantified savings are not asserted.
projects.summary: I identified inefficiencies in everyday business operations and developed AI-enabled workflows to improve employee access to information, task tracking and internal communication.

chapters.label: Business context
chapters.title: Business context
paragraphs: As EMotorad expanded its operations, employees needed access to internal processes, training materials and standard operating procedures. Managers also needed visibility into pending work, task ownership and completion deadlines.
Through ARCHMATION, I identified opportunities to simplify these activities using existing business tools and automated workflows.

chapters.label: Understanding the problem
chapters.title: Understanding the problem
paragraphs: Employees depended on colleagues and managers for routine questions about internal processes and SOPs. Training materials and process documentation required employees to search through multiple resources. Tracking pending activities, communicating deadlines and following up on incomplete tasks involved repetitive manual coordination.

chapters.label: Developing the solutions
chapters.title: Developing the solutions
paragraphs: Employee knowledge and training — I developed a workflow to organise internal documentation, SOPs and training materials into an accessible knowledge base. Employees could retrieve relevant information through natural-language queries, reducing dependence on individual team members.

Task tracking and operational visibility — I developed workflows to consolidate pending activities, assigned responsibilities, completion dates and task status. Managers could review outstanding work without manually collecting updates from multiple employees.

Automated reminders and follow-ups — I designed automated notifications through WhatsApp and Gmail for upcoming deadlines, incomplete activities and pending responses. Reminders were linked to task status and completion dates.

chapters.label: Implementation approach
chapters.title: Implementation approach
paragraphs: I used n8n to connect existing business applications, organise information and automate recurring activities. The workflows were designed around familiar communication channels to minimise changes to employees’ daily routines.
My contribution covered identifying operational gaps, defining workflow requirements, selecting integrations and developing automation solutions.

chapters.title: Business context
paragraphs: Through ARCHMATION, I worked with businesses across industries on creative production requirements, including product photography, commercial videos, branding and architectural visualisation.

Conventional production involved photography, location arrangements, physical samples, 3D modelling and multiple rounds of revisions. These requirements affected production costs, turnaround times and the number of creative variations clients could explore.

chapters.label: Identifying commercial opportunities
chapters.title: Identifying commercial opportunities
paragraphs: I identified production activities where generative AI could reduce cost and effort while meeting client requirements.

Early experimentation revealed several limitations: inconsistent product appearance, inaccurate proportions, limited control over composition and difficulty maintaining visual consistency across multiple outputs.
I focused on developing repeatable workflows that addressed these limitations and could be adapted to different client requirements.

chapters.label: Developing commercial solutions

AI video production — Introduced generative video and AI presenter workflows for commercial videos, product demonstrations and branded communication, reducing dependence on conventional filming.

Architecture and design visualisation — Developed workflows for converting floor plans, reference images and design concepts into architectural visualisations, enabling faster exploration of design alternatives.
Branding and creative production — Developed reusable workflows for campaign imagery, moodboards, branded assets and creative variations while maintaining visual consistency.

chapters.label: Business context
chapters.title: Business context
paragraphs: Amazon's live learning programme generated substantial data through class attendance, assessment performance, practice activities and student interactions. Teachers needed to use this information to understand student performance and prepare subsequent classes.

chapters.label: Understanding the problem
chapters.title: Understanding the problem
paragraphs: Individual test scores provided limited visibility into which concepts students had misunderstood, how performance varied across a cohort and which topics required additional attention.
Teachers needed answers to specific questions:
• Which concepts are students struggling with?
• Which misconceptions are common across the class?
• Which students require additional support?
• Which topics should be revisited in the next session?
• How is student performance changing over time?

chapters.label: Defining the product
chapters.title: Defining the product
paragraphs: I defined a teacher insights framework connecting assessment results, engagement data and knowledge graph mappings.

The dashboard organised student performance across individual concepts, difficulty levels and cohorts. Teachers could identify knowledge gaps, examine performance distributions, review frequently misunderstood concepts and identify students requiring targeted support.

chapters.label: Connecting insights to decisions
chapters.title: Connecting insights to decisions
paragraphs: I defined how dashboard insights could inform lesson preparation, revision sessions, targeted assessments and individual student interventions.
My contribution covered identifying teacher requirements, defining performance metrics, structuring the underlying information and translating analytical requirements into product specifications.

projects.problem: Developed personalised learning pathways based on user behaviour, proficiency and learning goals.
projects.summary: I defined the product logic for adaptive user journeys, connecting behavioural data, user segmentation and knowledge architecture to personalise individual experiences.

chapters.label: Business context
chapters.title: Business context
paragraphs: Students entered Amazon's learning platform with different academic goals, preparation levels, learning habits and time constraints. A standardised product journey could not adequately address these differences.
I identified opportunities to personalise how students entered the product, discovered relevant resources, progressed through subjects and received recommendations.

chapters.label: Understanding the problem
chapters.title: Understanding the problem
paragraphs: Several limitations affected the effectiveness of existing user journeys:
• Students with different preparation levels followed similar learning pathways.
• Students struggled to determine which topics to study next.
• Knowledge gaps and missing prerequisites affected progression.
• Assessment performance was not consistently connected to subsequent recommendations.
• Students with limited time needed different learning pathways from those following comprehensive preparation programmes.

chapters.label: Defining user personas
chapters.title: Defining user personas
paragraphs: I developed four behavioural personas to inform product journeys and recommendations.

chapters.label: Building adaptive product logic
chapters.title: Building adaptive product logic
paragraphs: I defined how assessment performance, recent activity, preparation stage, individual goals and knowledge graph relationships could influence each student's journey.
The progression framework incorporated two mechanisms:
• Strict gates: Require essential prerequisite knowledge before advancing.
• Soft checkpoints: Recommend revision or additional practice while allowing students to continue.
This allowed the product to balance structured progression with individual user preferences.

chapters.label: My contribution
chapters.title: My contribution
paragraphs: I defined the user segmentation framework, progression logic, diagnostic requirements, remediation pathways and personalised recommendation criteria, collaborating with product and technical teams on their integration into the learning experience.

projects.title: Improving speed, quality and efficiency at scale.
projects.problem: Redesigned editorial production and quality assessment processes across multiple content formats.
projects.summary: I transformed complex operational workflows by introducing structured quality frameworks, automated validation and continuous feedback mechanisms.

chapters.label: Business context
chapters.title: Business context
paragraphs: Amazon's learning platform required the continuous development, review and publication of thousands of learning resources. As production volumes increased, maintaining accuracy, meeting publishing deadlines and coordinating multiple specialised teams became increasingly complex.
I led initiatives to improve production workflows, quality standards and operational performance.

chapters.label: Understanding the problem
chapters.title: Understanding the problem
paragraphs: I identified several recurring operational bottlenecks:
• Inconsistent submission standards across production teams.
• Repeated review cycles caused by errors identified late in the process.
• Subjective quality assessments and inconsistent reviewer feedback.
• Manual verification of formatting, completeness and compliance.
• Limited visibility into production bottlenecks and recurring errors.
• Repetition of previously identified mistakes across subsequent submissions.

chapters.label: Redesigning operational workflows
chapters.title: Redesigning operational workflows
paragraphs: I introduced standardised submission requirements, quality checkpoints and acceptance criteria across different stages of production.
Review processes were restructured to identify errors earlier, clarify reviewer responsibilities and reduce unnecessary handovers.

chapters.label: Establishing quality and feedback systems
chapters.title: Establishing quality and feedback systems
paragraphs: I developed quality frameworks that classified errors by type, severity and frequency. Recurring errors informed updates to production guidelines, team training and review checklists.

Automated validation addressed repetitive checks involving formatting, missing information and submission requirements. Specialist reviewers concentrated on accuracy and issues requiring professional judgement.

chapters.label: My contribution
chapters.title: My contribution
paragraphs: I led process analysis, workflow improvements, quality framework development and performance monitoring. I coordinated production and quality teams, using error patterns, review data and turnaround times to identify further improvements.
